title: The Room of Marrow Creek
premise: Cyrus Vasquez arrives in Marrow Creek to teach at a school where a child vanishes from every graduating class, and the town's polite silence is a covenant older than anyone will admit. When his own sleep recordings reveal a second voice answering questions he never asked aloud, Cyrus discovers the town survives by feeding one memory-bearing child each winter to the frost — and that his late sister was one of them. As the count approaches and his own students begin sleepwalking toward the ridge, Cyrus must choose between the loyalty that keeps the town alive and the truth that could free it. In the end he breaks the covenant by giving the frost his own name instead, trading his identity for the children's, and the final chapter shows Marrow Creek thawing while a teacher with no remembered past walks out of the school and into the snow.
about_author: Ines Yarrow is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent a decade collecting local disappearance legends across the northern counties before turning them into fiction. She writes in unheated farmhouses, insisting the cold keeps the prose honest.

chapters.title: The Welcome Sign Was Repainted
chapters.summary: Cyrus Vasquez arrives in Marrow Creek, noting the freshly painted welcome sign and the way conversations stop when he enters rooms. POV: Cyrus. Beat: unease dressed as hospitality; the reader senses the town is performing normalcy for his benefit.

chapters.title: Twenty-Three Desks
chapters.summary: On his first teaching day, Cyrus counts twenty-three desks but the roster lists twenty-two students, and no one will explain the extra chair. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the first crack in the town's facade, and his professional instinct to explain it away begins its long losing argument.

chapters.title: What the Class Won't Say
chapters.summary: A student, Wren Halloway, draws the same frost pattern on every assignment and tells Cyrus the ridge 'counts' each year. POV: Wren. Beat: dread through a child's matter-of-fact voice; the missing-class problem becomes personal rather than rumor.

chapters.title: The Previous Teacher's Closet
chapters.summary: Cyrus finds his predecessor's abandoned belongings, including a box of cassette tapes labeled with dates and the word LISTEN. POV: Cyrus. Beat: temptation; he chooses curiosity over the town's unspoken request to leave things alone.

chapters.title: The Noises Have Explanations
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: young Cyrus convincing himself, for twenty years, that every unexplained sound in his life had a rational cause, including the night his sister disappeared. POV: Cyrus (memory). Beat: establishes his coping mechanism and the wound beneath it.

chapters.title: Sleep Recording, Night One
chapters.summary: Cyrus records himself sleeping to prove the noises are his own; the playback captures a second voice calmly answering questions he never asked. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the rationalist framework shatters; terror arrives not as a scream but as a conversation.

chapters.title: The Voice Asks Back
chapters.summary: The voice begins asking Cyrus questions about his sister, using details only she knew. POV: Cyrus. Beat: grief weaponized; he realizes the thing on the tape is not impersonating her — it may be collecting her.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Marrow Creek
chapters.summary: The diner owner, Ada, finally explains: each winter the town gives the ridge one child, and in exchange no one else dies of the cold. POV: Ada. Beat: the horror reframes as complicity; loyalty and survival are revealed as the same bargain.

chapters.title: Wren's Name Is on the List
chapters.summary: Cyrus learns the count is due before the first hard frost, and Wren has been chosen — her family took payment years ago. POV: Wren. Beat: the abstract covenant gains a face; Cyrus's teacher instinct collides with town law.

chapters.title: The Parents Who Paid
chapters.summary: Wren's parents beg Cyrus not to interfere, revealing the payment bought their other child's surgery. POV: Wren's mother, briefly; mostly Cyrus observing. Beat: the price of survival made concrete; no villain, only arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Ridge at Dusk
chapters.summary: Cyrus hikes toward the ridge against warnings and finds a field of frost patterns, each one shaped like a child's name he can almost read. POV: Cyrus. Beat: awe and horror fused; the frost is not weather but a ledger.

chapters.title: The School Remembers
chapters.summary: The empty classroom's twenty-third desk appears in Cyrus's own apartment, and the voice on the tape begins speaking in his sister's cadence full-time. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the haunting follows him home; his identity as an outsider starts dissolving.

chapters.title: What Ada Buried
chapters.summary: Ada confesses her own daughter was given to the ridge forty years ago and that she has kept the count ever since; she begs Cyrus to let Wren go so the ledger stays balanced. POV: Ada. Beat: tragic symmetry — the keeper of the covenant was once its victim's mother.

chapters.title: The Sleepwalking Class
chapters.summary: Half the class begins sleepwalking toward the ridge at night, drawn by the count's approach; Cyrus catches them at the treeline in the snow. POV: Cyrus. Beat: escalation from one child at risk to many; time collapses.

chapters.title: The Voice Offers a Trade
chapters.summary: The second voice proposes a substitution: a name for a name, a memory for a child. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the temptation chapter — he could save everyone by erasing himself, and part of him wants to be erased.

chapters.title: Wren Refuses to Be Saved
chapters.summary: Wren tells Cyrus she's willing to go, believing her sacrifice will protect her little brother forever. POV: Wren. Beat: heartbreaking loyalty; the children have absorbed the town's arithmetic more completely than the adults.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Count
chapters.summary: The town gathers for the quiet ritual of preparation; Cyrus watches neighbors he's come to care for light candles for a child they are giving away. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the loyalty vs. truth theme at full pressure — he loves these people and knows what they are.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes Its Final Pattern
chapters.summary: On the ridge, the count begins; frost spreads in the shape of names, and Wren walks forward while the town watches from below. POV: alternating Cyrus and Wren. Beat: climax opens; the ledger demands payment and the town holds its breath.

chapters.title: A Name for a Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus steps between Wren and the frost and speaks his own name into the pattern, offering his memories, his past, his sister's name — everything — in exchange. POV: Cyrus. Beat: climax and sacrifice; the rationalist finally surrenders the only thing he has left, his story.

chapters.title: The Thaw
chapters.summary: The frost recedes for the first time in a century; the ridge goes silent, the twenty-third desk vanishes, and Wren wakes in her own bed. POV: Wren. Beat: release and wonder; the children are free, but no one can find Cyrus.

chapters.title: The Teacher with No Yesterday
chapters.summary: A man walks out of the school with no memories, no name, and no grief; Wren recognizes his coat and decides to tell him a kinder story about who he was. POV: Wren. Beat: bittersweet resolution; identity is shown to be a story the living tell on behalf of the lost.

chapters.title: Marrow Creek, After
chapters.summary: One year later: the school has a full roster, the recordings are blank, and a new teacher named Cyrus — renamed by Wren — hangs a welcome sign he doesn't remember painting. POV: Cyrus (newly himself). Beat: quiet coda; the town keeps its secret, but the count is broken, and survival has finally stopped costing children.
